summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, and fever following recent bilateral toe amputations for dry gangrene. Initially treated for possible pneumonia, she was found to have Influenza A and was started on oseltamivir. Her asthma exacerbated by the flu was managed with increased prednisone and nebulizers, with gradual tapering as symptoms improved. Antibiotics were discontinued due to lack of evidence for bacterial pneumonia. She was stabilized on the medical floor, weaned off oxygen, and her leukocytosis and hyponatremia improved. Hypertension was managed with the addition of amlodipine. She was discharged home with home health services, on a short prednisone taper, new antihypertensive, and instructions to take an extra dose of furosemide to address mild fluid overload. Follow-up was arranged for lab monitoring and vascular surgery.
